doc: Python's builtin types, and how the symbolic types are spelled in them.

notes.i64: Python integers have no width, so this spelling accepts values the wire will not carry. Anything beyond 64 bits is refused at the boundary rather than truncated.
notes.bool: A `bool` is an `int` in Python, so a value meant as a number can arrive as True. The boundary check catches it.
notes.bytes: Base64 text, since JSON has no byte string and a proof is handed what JSON gives it. Decode it with `base64.b64decode`.

types.name: int
types.doc: An integer of unbounded size. Values beyond 64 bits do not fit the wire and travel as text.

types.name: Decimal
types.doc: An exact decimal, which travels as text so that no digits are lost on the way.

types.name: datetime
types.doc: An instant, which travels as an ISO 8601 string.

types.name: tuple_immutable
types.doc: Python tuples are immutable where lists are not; both arrive as JSON arrays.
